content.overview: BNS s. 241 — Destruction of document or electronic record to prevent its production as evidence.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Destruction of document or electronic record to prevent its production as evidence. BNS restatement of IPC 205. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 205. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 241 is the rule on “Destruction of document or electronic record to prevent its production as evidence”. The section provides that whoever secretes or destroys any document or electronic record which he may be lawfully compelled to produce as evidence in a Court or in any proceeding lawfully held before a public servant, as such, or obliterates or renders illegible the whole or any part of such document or electronic record with the intention of preventing the same from being produced or used as evidence before such Court or public servant as aforesaid, or after he shall have been lawfully summoned or required to produce the same for that purpose, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 241 exists so that “Destruction of document or electronic record to prevent its production as evidence” has a closed legal test in Chapter XIV — Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Perjury, screening, harbouring, false charge, and failing to appear on a bond.
